title: Sample-Efficient Tabular Self-Play for Offline Robust Reinforcement Learning
provenance_note: The SHA-256 identifies the exact retained PDF inspected in this rapid source/argument check. Original supplied report bytes are retained locally. The original PDF retrieval timestamp is taken from matching retained metadata.
version: NeurIPS 2025 official proceedings PDF (retained local copy)
summary: A fully covered two-stage game makes the paper’s gap zero while a player has a profitable unilateral deviation. Separate defects affect the printed supremum TV dual, an unrestricted adaptive concentration lemma and the lower-bound recursion. The current implementation uses a correct supremum structure but its nominal joint-value metric does not measure robust equilibrium regret.
impact_rationale: Major: the central equilibrium certificate and returned cross-game strategy pair fail a concrete admissible game. Independent substantial proof defects also prevent reading the stated rate as an established robust-Nash guarantee.

problems.title: Zero printed gap can conceal a profitable unilateral deviation
problems.source_location: Section 2, Eqs.(6),(8)–(9), PDF pp.4–5; Algorithm 2, p.8; Theorem 4.2, pp.8–9
claim:
Let \(L(\mu,
u)=\inf_P V^{\mu,
u,P}\) and \(U(\mu,
u)=\sup_P V^{\mu,
u,P}\), using the two players’ prescribed uncertainty sets. Their utilities are \((L,-U)\). Equation (9) substitutes reference equilibrium values for current joint-policy values, and Algorithm 2 combines the maximizing strategy of one zero-sum game with the minimizing strategy of another.
analysis:
True unilateral regret is \[\max\{\max_{\mu'}L(\mu',
u)-L(\mu,
u),\ U(\mu,
u)-\min_{
u'}U(\mu,
u')\}.\] Separate robust envelopes need not form a common zero-sum payoff, even with equal radii.

Take horizon \(2\), states \(s_0,s_1\), two actions per player, and both radii \(1/4\). At time \(1\), at either state set \[R=\begin{pmatrix}3/20&7/20\\1/2&7/10\end{pmatrix},\qquad P(s_1)=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&1/2\\0&0\end{pmatrix}.\] At time \(2\), reward is \(0\) at \(s_0\) and \(1\) at \(s_1\), independent of actions. Direct binary TV optimization gives \[L=\begin{pmatrix}2/5&3/5\\1/2&7/10\end{pmatrix},\qquad U=\begin{pmatrix}9/10&11/10\\3/4&19/20\end{pmatrix}.\] Row \(2\) strictly dominates for \(L\); column \(1\) strictly dominates for minimizing \(U\). The actual equilibrium is \((2,1)\), with reference values \(L^*=1/2,U^*=3/4\).

The separate zero-sum saddles are \((2,1)\) for \(L\) and \((1,1)\) for \(U\). The crossed output is \((1,1)\). Its maximizing-player regret is \(1/2-2/5=1/10\), while minimizing-player regret is zero. Yet the paper’s gap is \(\max\{1/2-1/2,\ 3/4-9/10\}=0\). Interpreting \(U^*\) instead as the separate minimax value \(9/10\) also gives zero.

Uniform initial states and uniform behavior policies give time-one joint occupancies \(1/8\), and time-two joint occupancies \(3/16\) and \(1/16\). Thus \(d_m^n=1/16>0\); the clipped numerator is at most \(1/8\), yielding \(C_r^*\le2\). Sample thresholds can be met by increasing the number of trajectories. The calculation grants correct zero terminal values, exact transitions and vanishing bonuses; strict best-response inequalities persist under sufficiently small estimation errors.
result: The printed certificate does not characterize absence of profitable unilateral deviations, and the exact-model crossed strategy output need not be a robust Nash equilibrium. This rejects the usual equilibrium interpretation of the rate, rather than a numerical bound on the paper’s weaker printed gap. Uncertainty-free common-payoff games remain a valid special case.
repair: Use actual robust current-policy values in both unilateral regrets. A known-model backward construction can solve the corresponding bimatrix game with utilities given by each player’s own robust continuation payoff. Its offline statistical rate and computation require a new analysis; replacing a solver does not preserve the stated theorem automatically.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Major: an admissible, fully covered game violates the core equilibrium interpretation even with exact model knowledge.

problems.title: The printed supremum TV dual clips in the wrong direction
problems.source_location: Appendix B.1, Lemma B.1, Eq.(27b), PDF p.23; Eq.(17), p.7
claim: Equation (27b) minimizes \(p^\top[V]_\alpha-\sigma(\alpha-\max_s[V]_\alpha(s))\), with upper clipping \([V]_\alpha=\min(V,\alpha)\) and \(\alpha\in[\min V,\max V]\).
analysis: The maximum clipped entry equals \(\alpha\), so the penalty vanishes; minimizing gives \(\min V\), regardless of \(p,\sigma\). For \(p=(1/2,1/2),V=(0,1),\sigma=1/4\), the printed result is \(0\). Feasible distributions are \(q=(1-t,t)\), with \(t\in[1/4,3/4]\), so the actual supremum is \(3/4\).
result: The general displayed dual is false. The current author source provides important counterevidence: alpha_min_backup uses lower clipping, and the policy routines obtain a supremum by negating an infimum of the negative value vector. Those structural implementations are consistent with the correct operation and were not executed here.
repair: The correct full-simplex dual, with \(m=\min V,M=\max V\), is \[\sup_{\operatorname{TV}(q,p)\le\sigma}q^\top V=\min_{\alpha\in[m,M]}\{p^\top\max(V,\alpha)+\sigma(M-\alpha)\}.\] It follows by applying the valid infimum formula to \(M\mathbf1-V\) and substituting \(\alpha=M-t\). On the binary example its minimum is \(3/4\).
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Major: this is a universally stated Bellman-duality identity with a large exact counterexample, although the corresponding current source structure is already correct.

problems.title: Nominal joint value does not measure unilateral robust regret
problems.source_location: Section 5, PDF p.10; main.py, generate_VI, figure_wrt_samples and evaluate_policies
claim: The experiments support equilibrium learning, but the available script compares nominal joint-policy values to a nominal baseline, without computing robust current values or unilateral best responses.
analysis: For the one-step game \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\), let \(\mu=(1,0)\), \(\nu=(1/2,1/2)\). The joint value and equilibrium value are both \(1/2\), so the released absolute-value score is zero. The minimizing player can switch to column \(2\), reducing its cost to \(0\); regret is \(1/2\). Positive uncertainty radii do not affect a one-step payoff. Statically, generate_VI never uses its sigma argument; evaluate_policies performs expected nominal backups; figure_wrt_samples compares those joint values. The snapshot also differs from the paper in action count, seed count and numerical framework.
result: The available metric cannot certify robust Nash regret. It can legitimately describe joint-value error. The exact producing code and run histories for the published curves are not established by this snapshot, so the paper’s numerical curves are not declared fabricated or reproduced.
repair: Evaluate each player’s robust current value and its robust best response to the fixed opponent, then report both regrets. Existing joint-value error can remain a separate descriptive metric.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Minor: a confirmed current-release metric mismatch, with historical benchmark provenance and resulting policy quality unresolved.

problems.title: The concentration rate cannot cover every bounded adaptive vector
problems.source_location: Lemma D.1, Eq.(46), PDF p.27; dependence discussion, p.28; Appendix G.1, p.51
claim: The lemma permits any \(V\) with \(\|V\|_\infty\le H\), explicitly without independence from the empirical transition row, but gives an empirical-Bernstein rate without a state-dimension term.
analysis: For uniform \(p_i=1/S\), take empirical frequencies \(\hat p\) from \(N\) independent categorical draws and choose \(I=\{i:\hat p_i>1/S\}\), \(V_i=H\mathbf1_{\{i\in I\}}\), \(\sigma=1/(2S)\). If \(\hat p\ne p\), both masses of the nonempty excess set exceed \(\sigma\). Binary TV minimization gives \[\inf_{q\in U_\sigma(\hat p)}q^\top V-\inf_{q\in U_\sigma(p)}q^\top V=H\operatorname{TV}(\hat p,p),\] while \(\operatorname{Var}_{\hat p}V\le H^2/4\).

For completeness set \(Z=\operatorname{TV}(\hat p,p)\) and let \(Y=X-N/S\), \(X\sim\operatorname{Bin}(N,1/S)\), with variance \(v=N(S-1)/S^2\ge1\). The fourth moment is at most \(4v^2\); Hölder gives \(\mathbb E|Y|\ge\sqrt v/2\). Hence \(\mathbb EZ\ge\frac14\sqrt{(S-1)/N}\). Changing one observation changes \(Z\) by at most \(1/N\); Efron–Stein gives variance at most \(1/(2N)\). Chebyshev therefore gives \[\Pr\{Z\ge\tfrac18\sqrt{(S-1)/N}\}\ge1-\frac{32}{S-1}.\]

For polynomially large \(N,K\) satisfying burn-in conditions, the proposed right side is at most \[C_4H\sqrt{\log(KH/\delta)/(4N)}+C_4H\log(KH/\delta)/N\]. Any universal \(C_4\) is eventually defeated by the state-dimension factor above. The row example embeds in a full-coverage model with uniform states and transition rows; conditioning on its row count preserves uniform independent next states. It is not asserted that Algorithm 2 produces this particular adaptive vector. Appendix G.1 instead begins with a fixed independent vector and does not supply the claimed independence-removal step.
result: The unrestricted adaptive-vector lemma is false at the stated rate. An algorithm-specific leave-one-out or stability proof could still establish a suitably restricted rate, but is not supplied by the displayed fixed-vector argument.
repair: Restrict the lemma to an independent vector and separately establish the independence or dependence control needed for the actual algorithmic iterates. No replacement algorithm-specific rate is claimed here.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Major: the explicitly unrestricted lemma fails dimensionally and is used to justify the core sample-complexity proof.

problems.title: The hard-family recursion overlooks other zero-valued absorbing states
problems.source_location: Appendix E.1, Eqs.(86)–(100), PDF pp.37–38; Lemma E.2, Eq.(94); Appendix H.1, pp.59–60
claim: Equation (86) makes every \(m_j\), \(j\ne f\), an absorbing zero-reward state. The full-simplex TV set in Eq.(89) can move mass to those states, while Eq.(94b) assumes its adverse mass moves to \(m_f\).
analysis: Take states \((m_f,n_f,m_j,n_j)\), horizon \(H=16\), two actions, \(c_0=1/4,c_1=1/8,c_2=1/4,\sigma=1/2\), \[p=129/256,\quad \Delta=1/1024,\quad q=515/1024.\] These satisfy \(p>q\ge1/2\), \(H>16\log2\), \(\sigma\le1-c_0\), \(\sigma>c_2/(2H)\), \(\Delta\le c_1\sigma/H\) and \(p+\Delta\le1\). Choose any admissible packing vector and its good action at \(m_f\).

At time \(H\), values are \((0,1,0,1)\). At time \(H-1\), robust values are \((1/256,3/2,0,3/2)\). At \(H-2\), nature can shift mass \(1/2\) from the absorbing \(n_f\) to \(m_j\), at TV distance exactly \(1/2\). Since \(m_j\) has value zero, this is optimal and gives \(V_{H-2}(n_f)=7/4\). Equation (94b) instead adds \(\sigma V_{H-1}(m_f)=1/512\), yielding \(897/512\). The same omitted destination affects Eq.(94a).
result: The literal hard-family recursion and its claimed minimum-state ordering are false. Equation (98) describes a different nonabsorbing background family and is relevant evidence of possible intended wording; adopting it would require coordinated reconstruction of the construction and proof. This finding does not rule out a similar lower-bound rate from another family.
repair: For the displayed family and \(q\ge\sigma\), write \(u_h=p\mu_h(\phi_h\mid m_f)+q\mu_h(1-\phi_h\mid m_f)\). The corrected recursions are \[V_h(m_j)=0,\quad V_h(n_i)=1+(1-\sigma)V_{h+1}(n_i),\] \[V_h(m_f)=(u_h-\sigma)V_{h+1}(n_f)+(1-u_h)V_{h+1}(m_f).\] Induction keeps the \(n_i\) tied and highest-valued, while \(m_j\) remains a minimum; moving adverse mass there verifies the formulas. The information-theoretic separation, coverage and rate must then be reanalyzed.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Major: an exact counterexample invalidates a substantive dynamic-programming lemma used by the claimed matching lower bound.
